candidates: When a function or regex is documented to handle nested structures only up to a fixed depth (e.g., 'up to N levels of nested parentheses'), the test suite must include at least one case that exercises that stated maximum depth—relying solely on shallow or typical cases that fall well within the limit leaves the documented boundary unverified.

When using a depth-limited regex to parse nested structures (instead of a CSS parser or a recursive matcher), add an inline comment that states both the nesting depth limit and why the heavier alternative was not chosen (e.g., runtime performance sensitivity); during review, explicitly assess whether the stated depth is sufficient for realistic inputs the project will encounter.
